name: cli-init-refuse-existing
body: `kalide init` guards against clobbering: it fails (clear message, non-zero exit, nothing written) if `slides/`, `assets/` or `kalide.yaml` already exists — in every branch. An existing local `templates/` blocks init only in the built-in starter-deck branch (no path and no configured default, or `--local`), where the seed writes a local `templates/`. In the external-library branch (an explicit `path` or the configured default, init-library-resolution) a pre-existing local `templates/` is exempt from the check: init proceeds, writes the deck referencing the external library, and the local `templates/` is left in place and untouched (never deleted, never overwritten) — it participates as the deck's local library layer that `kalide start` loads (layered-template-library). A pre-existing `AGENTS.md` at the target is not a blocking path: it never blocks init, in any branch, and it is handled per agent-guide-reference — left byte-for-byte untouched when it already carries the string `Kalide Reference: ./AGENTS_KALIDE.md`, and otherwise the reference line is appended with its other bytes preserved. A pre-existing `AGENTS_KALIDE.md` likewise never blocks init; the deck full guide is written to `AGENTS_KALIDE.md` only when that file is absent (see cli-init, agent-guide-reference, agent-authoring). Other files (e.g. `.git`) do not block. There is no `--force` flag.
